newsitem.title: USA: PGA GOLF-LOW HOPES BUT HIGH RESULTS FOR LEHMAN IN FIRST ROUND.
newsitem.headline: PGA GOLF-LOW HOPES BUT HIGH RESULTS FOR LEHMAN IN FIRST ROUND.

text.p: Tom Lehman thinks
his low expectatioins for he game may have helped him to the
six under par 66 to lead the first round at the Mercedes
Championships on Thursday.
Lehman finished a stroke ahead of Paul Goydos and Jim
Furyk, who had 67s. At three under 69 were Fred Couples, Guy
Boros and Justin Leonard.
Tiger Woods led a group of eight players at two under par
The Mercedes is the opening event in the PGA Tour's 1997
season, with 32 winners of 1996 tournaments composing the
field.
Lehman is playing as though there was no two-month gap
since the last official event -- the '96 Tour Championship,
which he won by six strokes.
"I started slow, didn't feel really focused," Lehman
said. "But I made a bogey on the fifth hole, and that got me
back into the competitive mode, and I made seven birdies in 13
holes.
"The key to the round was that I didn't expect too much of
myself. I didn't practice that much during the off-season.
There was no pressure to play well, no huge expectations. But
once you start making a few putts, the hole starts looking
bigger and it all gets a bit easier."
Lehman, the British Open champion, the 1996 money leader
and Vardon Trophy winner, is expected to be named PGA Tour
Player of the Year at Friday night's award ceremony here.
"I just came out and winged it," Goydos said. "I didn't
have any real expectations. Then I made three birdie putts
over 30 feet on the front nine, which may be more than I made
all last year, and just had a really good putting day."
Furyk was the only one of the leaders to have a
bogey-free round. Although he, too, did very little work on
his game in the off-season, Furyk said that his advantage came
from being rested and refreshed mentally.
